articles.headline: Mookie Betts homers twice and Dodgers hit 4 in 8th inning of 8-2 win over Giants
articles.description: — Mookie Betts homered twice and the Los Angeles Dodgers went deep four times in the eighth inning of an 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
articles.headlineJa: ムーキー・ベッツが2本塁打、ドジャースが8回に4発叩き込みジャイアンツに8-2で勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜の試合で、ムーキー・ベッツが2本の本塁打を放ち、ロサンゼルス・ドジャースが8回に4本塁打を集めてサンフランシスコ・ジャイアンツに8-2で勝利した。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Mookie Betts homered twice and the Los Angeles Dodgers went deep four times in the eighth inning of an 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.


              Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker connected back-to-back in the eighth. Betts and Max Muncy added two-out solo shots in a five-run inning as the NL West champions rolled in a series opener between old rivals.


              Tyler Glasnow (5-1) allowed two runs and three hits in six innings with a season-high 10 strikeouts.


              The home run barrage occurred on the 20th anniversary of the Dodgers' four-plus-one game. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin and Marlon Anderson hit four consecutive homers in the bottom of the ninth inning — the fourth time in major league history the feat had been accomplished.


              Giants reliever Philip Abner gave up all five runs in the eighth, which began with the Dodgers leading 3-2. He became the second reliever in Giants history to give up four homers in one inning.


              The Giants (64-90) lost their 90th game, their most since 2017 when they dropped 98.


              Muncy’s shot traveled 420 feet and Tucker’s went 403 feet, both to right-center. Betts also homered leading off the game.


              Josue De Paula, a 21-year-old Dodgers rookie finishing his first week in the major leagues, lined a two-out double to right field for the go-ahead run in the sixth. He also singled and scored the tying run on Teoscar Hernández’s RBI single in the fifth. 


              Edwin Díaz struck out two in a scoreless ninth in his return from the injured list.


              The Giants tied the game at 1 on Jung Hoo Lee's leadoff homer in the second and went ahead 2-1 on Jonah Cox's RBI single with two outs in the third.


              Giants starter Cesar Perdomo gave up two runs and six hits in 4 2/3 innings with one strikeout. Jason Foley (3-2) took the loss in relief.


              Giants first baseman Bryce Eldridge was a late scratch with a head laceration.


              Up next
              The Giants had yet to announce a starter for Saturday against Dodgers LHP Tarik Skubal (10-7, 2.70 ERA).


              ------

During the final stretch of the MLB regular season, some teams are already thinking about October while others are locked in tight pennant races. 

The Tampa Bay Rays, Milwaukee Brewers, Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Yankees and Atlanta Braves all have clinched postseason spots. The Braves secured their spot on Friday with a win over the Astros.

The Boston Red Sox and Chicago Cubs are also on their ways to securing playoff spots in the coming days.

Beyond those top teams, there are many storylines to watch down the stretch: Where do current playoff matchups stand? Which games should you be watching each day leading up to October? Who will clinch next? And what does the playoff schedule look like?

Here's everything you need to know for the homestretch.

The Cubs, Red Sox and Phillies all could clinch their spots this weekend.

Breaking down the AL race

The Rays and Yankees are battling for the AL East crown with the Red Sox also very likely to be playing in October. The Chicago White Sox and Cleveland Guardians are in a tight race for the AL Central title, and the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers are part of a muddled AL West and wild-card picture.

The Brewers and Dodgers have both clinched their divisions, while the Braves also have a comfortable division lead, so any NL intrigue will likely come in the wild-card races. The Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies have separated themselves there, with the San Diego Padres and Arizona Diamondbacks battling for the other spot.

articles.headline: Ty France's 3-run homer helps Padres to 8-2 win over Marlins and into tie for top NL wild-card spot
articles.description: — Ty France hit a three-run homer to cap a six-run rally in the fifth inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 8-2 on Friday night to pull into a tie with Philadelphia and Chicago for the top National League wild card.
articles.headlineJa: タイ・フランスの3ラン本塁打でパドレスがマーリンズに8-2で勝利、ナ・リーグのワイルドカード首位タイに浮上
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜の試合で、タイ・フランスが5回裏の6得点の猛攻を締めくくる3ラン本塁打を放ち、サンディエゴ・パドレスがマイアミ・マーリンズを8-2で破り、フィラデルフィアおよびシカゴと並んでナショナル・リーグのワイルドカード首位タイに躍り出た。
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — Ty France hit a three-run homer to cap a six-run rally in the fifth inning and the San Diego Padres beat the Miami Marlins 8-2 on Friday night to pull into a tie with Philadelphia and Chicago for the top National League wild card.


              The Cubs and Phillies both lost just around first pitch in San Diego. Then the Padres erased a 1-0 deficit to win for the 11th time in 12 games. 


              Although Chicago, Philadelphia and San Diego are even at 85-69 for the three NL wild cards, the Padres would lose tiebreakers against the Cubs and Phillies in the race for the No. 1 spot and the right to host an opening round. The Cubs beat the Padres 2-1 in the wild-card round in Chicago last season.


              Miami (76-78) was eliminated from the postseason race.


              France, who signed a minor league deal during spring training, hit the first pitch he saw from reliever Tyler Zuber off the balcony on the third level of the Western Metal Supply Co. brick warehouse in the left-field corner with two outs in the fifth to bring in Fernando Tatis Jr. and Dustin Harris to make it 6-1.


              France paused for a moment to watch his career-high 21st homer sail away and then tossed his bat and began his trot. France played at San Diego State for Hall of Famer Tony Gwynn and is in his second stint with the Padres. 


              Tatis hit an RBI single with the bases loaded and one out, and Harris followed with a two-run single. 


              Agustín Ramírez, Miami's No. 9 batter, lined a homer off Nick Pivetta into the seats in left field with one out in the third, his fifth. 


              That was the only big mistake by Pivetta (3-2), who allowed one run and four hits in five innings while striking out four and walking one. 


              San Diego's Jackson Merrill homered in the eighth, his 26th.


              Cade Gibson (5-2) took the loss in relief.


              Up next
              Marlins RHP Eury Pérez (7-11, 3.99 ERA) and Padres RHP Casey Mize (6-9, 3.69) are scheduled to start Saturday night. 


              ------

articles.headline: Ben Rice hits 39th homer, Cole becomes winningest No. 1 draft pick as Yanks cruise past D-backs 9-2
articles.description: — Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control early and beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 on Friday night.
articles.headlineJa: ベン・ライスが39号本塁打、コールがドラフト全体1位指名選手としての最多勝記録を更新、ヤンキースがDバックスに9-2で快勝
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜夜の試合で、ベン・ライスが今季39号本塁打を放ち、ゲリット・コールがドラフト全体1位指名選手としての通算最多勝投手となり、ニューヨーク・ヤンキースが初回に5点を奪って序盤から試合を優位に進め、アリゾナ・ダイヤモンドバックスに9-2で快勝した。
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- — Ben Rice hit his 39th homer of the season, Gerrit Cole became the winningest No. 1 overall draft pick and the New York Yankees used a five-run first inning to take control early and beat the Arizona Diamondbacks 9-2 on Friday night.


              After learning three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge was headed back to the injured list with a right calf strain, the Yankees won for the eighth time in 10 games. New York, which has already clinched a playoff spot, is four games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the AL East with nine games remaining.


              The D-backs' have lost three straight and their playoff hopes are in major trouble. They're five games back of the final NL wild card with eight games left.


              New York's first five batters reached against D-backs' All-Star left hander Eduardo Rodriguez and George Lombard Jr.'s two-run single made it 5-0. Lombard added a solo homer in the sixth and finished with three RBI.


              Cole (9-9) bounced back from a pair of starts that saw him surrender seven homers — the most he's ever given up over a two-game span. He gave up two runs and four hits in six innings, striking out six.


              Selected first by Pittsburgh in 2011, Cole won his 162nd game. That is one more than Mike Moore, picked No. 1 by Seattle in 1981.


              Rodriguez (15-7) picked a bad time to have arguably his worst start this season, needing 45 pitches to get three outs, his career high for a first inning. He gave up seven runs, five hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings.


              Corbin Carroll hit a two-run homer to cut the deficit to 5-2 in the second. Rice's solo homer in the third pushed the Yankees ahead 6-2.


              Up next
              The D-backs send RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77 ERA) to the mound Saturday night while the Yankees counter with RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95).


              ------

articles.headline: Heat, Pelle Larsson agree to 4-year, $60M extension
articles.description: The Heat and guard Pelle Larsson have reached agreement on a four-year, $60 million extension, his agents told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: ヒートとペレ・ラーソンが4年6000万ドルの延長契約に合意
articles.descriptionJa: ヒートとガードのペレ・ラーソンが4年6000万ドルの延長契約に合意したと、代理人がESPNのシャムズ・シャラニア記者に語りました。
articles.body:
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt in on 2030.

Larsson has become a foundation player for the Heat amid their offseason overhaul. He is set to have a major rotation role after averaging 11.4 points per game last season, up nearly seven points per game from his rookie season. Larsson also ranked fourth best in offensive efficiency in Miami, per ESPN Research, and fifth in minutes played.

Larsson started 54 of the 70 games he played last season and ranked in the top 10 in charges drawn last season, according to ESPN Research.

Miami's biggest offseason splash was the acquisition of Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade that saw a package headlined by Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. going back to Milwaukee. The Heat also signed free agent Klay Thompson after he cleared waivers following a buyout agreement with the Dallas Mavericks.

Miami looks to return to the postseason after missing the playoffs last season for the first time in seven seasons.
